issues.note: Commits 6b1a0a78 + 4af92188; live run against staging ipgrnwvfnumgvnxkpxsc — The prior verdict stands and was right: this was unbuilt ENGINEERING, and it is now built. Three things did not exist and now do. (1) No drafting path ever asked retrieve() for source_type='tender_document' - the only caller was the offline eval-corpus generator silver_baseline.py, which is why the corpus sat unread. (2) The regulatory block is deliberately UN-citable (renders no chunk_id, and tells the model the text is *"NEVER itself a citable source_id"*), so re-pointing it at a new source type could never have satisfied SC-14 - a new citable renderer emitting [TENDER-n] handles plus the RECORDED page/clause was required. (3) There was no citation bucket; build_source_citations now has a fourth, tender_chunk, additive so the three existing buckets are byte-identical for callers that do not pass it. Wired into draft_response AND the revision loop, so a revision RECOMPUTES its citations and cannot inherit one for text it no longer contains. Engine-owns-facts held strictly: the model's only contribution is which handle it marked; chunk_id, document_id, page, clause, quote and similarity are all copied from the engine's retrieval, so a hallucinated [TENDER-9] yields NO citation (asserted as an attack). A second, deterministic attribution route (>=8-word verbatim run) means provenance does not depend on model compliance. Contract scoping, with its limitation named: content_chunks has no contract column and retrieve() filters on org + source_type only, so without scoping a multi-contract org would cite ANOTHER bid's tender pack; document ids are resolved first and the fused set filtered on source_id. Because retrieve() truncates to top_k BEFORE returning, the fetch is widened 5x and BOTH counts (considered/kept) are recorded, so an over-run is measurable rather than looking like a clean miss. RELEASE WINDOW (--since 2026-07-29, covering Phase 1's 2026-08-02 ship and everything after): 110 deployments, all three projects, every walk exhausted=true - PREVIEW 98, EVERY ONE CANCELED; PRODUCTION 9 READY + 3 CANCELED, every one on ref=main. FULL HISTORY, cursor exhausted on all three projects (platform-web 66 pages/1,309 deployments back to 2026-03-18; internal 11 pages/204; portal 11 pages/204): 1,717 deployments, REAL EXIT 1, 438 billed non-main - and the dates are the finding: NOT ONE is inside this release, and only TWO post-date RULE 0 at all. 436 fall between 2026-03-18 and 2026-04-26, i.e. before RULE 0 existed (instituted 2026-05-05). R262-D-154's table fix HOLDS: the TABLE gap is 0. The 2 remaining group differences are the deliberately-excluded _deleted_orphan_* pair, correctly waived. WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT LAG — IT IS DIVERGENCE, AND THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY SAID OTHERWISE. The prior verdict says the gap *"is now ONE-DIRECTIONAL"* and *"an ordinary catch-up in one direction"*. That is true of TABLES and false of everything else: staging holds 35 objects production does not, and production holds 25 staging does not. ‼️ THREE COLUMNS EXIST ON PRODUCTION AND NOT ON STAGING, all on sso_provider_configs: acs_url, certificate, entity_id (prod 17 columns, staging 14) — SAML config that staging cannot store. ‼️ A DIFFERENT UNIQUE CONSTRAINT: production has sso_provider_configs_organisation_id_provider_type_key, staging has …_organisation_id_provider_name_key. The two databases enforce different uniqueness on the same table — staging accepts two configs sharing a provider_type, production rejects them, so an SSO test that passes on staging can fail on production and no gate would see it. ‼️ THREE TYPE FORKS: beta_invites.token prod text / staging uuid; nps_responses.score prod smallint / staging integer; help_search_logs.results_count prod smallint / staging integer; plus sso_provider_configs.supabase_sso_provider_id prod text / staging uuid. ‼️ 13 NULLABILITY FORKS, and they run BOTH WAYS, which is the dangerous shape — a NOT NULL on staging that production lacks means an insert that passes staging fails production, and vice versa: staging-stricter on account_deletion_queue.organisation_id, ai_usage.updated_at, evidence_tracker_state.{activated_at,created_at,updated_at}, nps_r
